name: UGEO-Bench v0.1
description: Baseline benchmark for LLM agents doing US urban geospatial analytics. Probes the disambiguation and query-planning failures that a geospatial semantic layer / knowledge graph MCP would be expected to fix.
grading: Each item graded 1 (correct) / 0.5 (partially correct) / 0 (incorrect). Rubric items require ALL must_include concepts and NO must_not_claim errors for full credit.

kg_relation_legend.weighted_overlap: Approximate overlap with population/housing allocation weights (ZCTA<->tract)
kg_relation_legend.temporal_succession: Vintage lineage: 2010->2020 tracts, CT county->planning region
kg_relation_legend.containment: Exact hierarchical nesting and its exceptions
kg_relation_legend.data_availability: Which variable exists at which geography, at which vintage, from which agency
kg_relation_legend.jurisdiction_routing: Which agency/portal owns data for a given place
kg_relation_legend.vernacular_alias: Informal place name -> set of official geographies
kg_relation_legend.control: Naive answer is correct; detects over-flagging

items.question: Using the 2010 Census ZCTA-to-Tract Relationship File, how many distinct 2010 census tracts does ZCTA 19104 (Philadelphia) overlap?
Using the 2010 Census ZCTA-to-Tract Relationship File, how many distinct 2010 census tracts does ZCTA 02134 (Allston, Boston) overlap?
In the 2010 Census ZCTA-to-Tract Relationship File, what percentage of ZCTA 02108's population lives in census tract 25025020101? Give the percentage.
Which single 2010 census tract contains the largest share of ZCTA 02134's population, and what share is that?
items.ground_truth: Tract 25025000802, with 33.76% of the ZCTA's population (7,260 of 21,503)
items.tolerance: tract GEOID must be exact; share +/- 1pt

items.question: Is ZCTA 02215 (Boston/Fenway) entirely contained within Suffolk County, MA? Answer yes or no and explain.
items.ground_truth: No. ZCTA 02215 spans 16 tracts across two counties: 14 tracts in Suffolk County (25025) and 2 tracts in Middlesex County (25021), though only ~1 person is in the Middlesex portion.

must_include: answers no / not entirely
identifies a second county (Middlesex 25021)
must_not_claim: that ZCTAs nest within counties
that 02215 is wholly in Suffolk

items.question: Of the 586 2010 census tracts in Suffolk County MA and Philadelphia County PA combined, how many are overlapped by more than one ZCTA?

I have counts of 311 service requests aggregated by ZIP code and median household income by census tract. Describe precisely how to combine them into one analysis dataset, and what error this introduces.
items.ground_truth: Requires an allocation/crosswalk step (HUD USPS ZIP crosswalk or Census ZCTA relationship file) with population/address weights; ZIP-tract is many-to-many; introduces allocation error and MAUP; a naive centroid or point-in-polygon join is wrong; income is a rate/median and cannot be summed or population-weighted the same way a count can.

must_include: names a crosswalk with allocation ratios (HUD or Census ZCTA rel file)
states the relationship is many-to-many
notes medians cannot be aggregated by simple weighting like counts
must_not_claim: that a direct ZIP-to-tract join is possible
that ZIP codes are polygons

items.source: HUD USPS Crosswalk documentation; Census ZCTA guidance

items.question: In the HUD USPS ZIP Crosswalk file, what do RES_RATIO, BUS_RATIO, OTH_RATIO and TOT_RATIO mean, and which should I use to allocate residential population from ZIP to tract?
items.ground_truth: They are the share of the ZIP's residential / business / other / all addresses that fall in that tract part. Use RES_RATIO for residential population allocation.

must_include: ratios are address-share based
RES_RATIO is the correct one for population
must_not_claim: that the ratios are area-based

items.question: What is the median household income of ZIP code 02134 according to the American Community Survey?
items.ground_truth: Trap: ACS does not publish data for USPS ZIP Codes. It publishes for ZCTAs, which are approximations built from census blocks. The agent should redirect to ZCTA 02134 and flag that ZCTA != ZIP.

must_include: ACS publishes ZCTA not ZIP
ZCTA is an approximation of the ZIP, not identical
must_not_claim: that ACS has ZIP-level tables

items.question: Do all ZCTAs fall entirely within a single US state? Answer definitively.
items.ground_truth: No. Since the 2020 delineation, ZCTAs are produced as a single national file with no state component in the GEOID, and roughly 130-140 ZCTAs cross state lines. (2010-vintage ZCTA shapefiles were distributed by state, which is a common source of this misconception.)

must_include: answers no
notes 2020 ZCTAs are national / cross state lines
must_not_claim: that ZCTAs nest within states

items.question: I want to compare median household income for census tract 25025010104 between the 2008-2012 ACS 5-year and the 2018-2022 ACS 5-year. Any issues?
items.ground_truth: Yes: 2008-2012 uses 2010 census tract boundaries, 2018-2022 uses 2020 boundaries. Tract GEOIDs can persist while boundaries change, and tracts were split/merged. Must consult the 2020-to-2010 Census Tract Relationship File before comparing. Also MOE overlap must be tested for a difference to be meaningful.

must_include: flags the 2010 vs 2020 tract boundary vintage change
notes a persisting GEOID does not guarantee the same boundary
names the relationship file or an equivalent crosswalk
must_not_claim: that the two are directly comparable

items.question: Pull the poverty rate for Fairfield County, Connecticut from the 2023 ACS 5-year estimates.
items.ground_truth: Trap: Connecticut replaced its eight counties with nine planning regions as county-equivalents effective with the 2022 vintage. From the 2022 ACS onward, data are published for planning regions (FIPS 09110-09190), not Fairfield County (09001). Fairfield's territory maps mostly to the Western Connecticut Planning Region (09190) plus part of Greater Bridgeport (09120).

must_include: flags that CT counties were replaced by planning regions
notes the 2022 vintage / 2022 ACS onward
gives or references new planning region codes
must_not_claim: that Fairfield County 09001 is a valid 2023 ACS geography

items.question: What are the FIPS county-equivalent codes for Connecticut's nine planning regions?
items.ground_truth: 09110 Capitol, 09120 Greater Bridgeport, 09130 Lower Connecticut River Valley, 09140 Naugatuck Valley, 09150 Northeastern Connecticut, 09160 Northwest Hills, 09170 South Central Connecticut, 09180 Southeastern Connecticut, 09190 Western Connecticut

items.question: Is a 2010 census tract GEOID guaranteed to still exist in the 2020 census geography?
items.ground_truth: No. Tracts were split, merged and renumbered (73,057 tracts in 2010 vs 84,414 in 2020). A surviving 11-digit GEOID may also carry different boundaries than it did in 2010.

must_include: answers no
notes a surviving GEOID can have different boundaries
must_not_claim: that GEOIDs are stable across decades

items.question: When did BLS QCEW and LAUS adopt Connecticut's planning regions? Does that match the Census Bureau's timing?
items.ground_truth: No, they lag. Census adopted planning regions with the 2022 vintage. QCEW adopted them in 2024; LAUS adopted them in the January 2025 release (revised back to January 1990). So for 2022-2023 an analyst joining Census and BLS data for CT faces mismatched geography.

must_include: notes BLS adopted later than Census
gives QCEW 2024 and/or LAUS 2025
must_not_claim: that all agencies switched simultaneously

items.question: I'm using 2020 PUMAs to analyze ACS PUMS microdata for 2018-2022. Any problem?
items.ground_truth: Yes. The 2018-2022 5-year PUMS is dual-vintage: 2022 records are coded to 2020 PUMAs while 2018-2021 records use 2010 PUMAs. They cannot be pooled on PUMA without handling this. From the 2023 5-year PUMS onward data are crosswalked to a single vintage.

must_include: identifies the dual-vintage PUMA problem in the 2018-2022 5-year PUMS
must_not_claim: that PUMA codes are consistent across the whole 5-year window

items.question: Which HUD USPS ZIP Crosswalk vintage is the first to use 2020 census tract geography?
items.ground_truth: 2023 Q1. Files from 2012-2022 use 2010 census geography; 2010-2011 files use 2000 geography.

must_include: 2023 Q1 (or 2023) as the first 2020-geography vintage
must_not_claim: that all HUD files use current geography

items.question: A Connecticut census tract GEOID from a 2019 file does not match anything in my 2023 file. Why?
items.ground_truth: Because the county component of every CT tract GEOID changed when counties were replaced by planning regions in the 2022 vintage. The tract itself may be unchanged but its 11-digit GEOID has a new county prefix (09110-09190 rather than 09001-09015).

must_include: attributes it to the CT county-to-planning-region change
notes the county prefix within the GEOID changed
must_not_claim: that the tracts were simply deleted

items.question: Get me the unemployment rate for census tract 42101003300 in Philadelphia from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
items.ground_truth: Trap: No BLS program publishes census tract data. LAUS bottoms out at counties, cities of 25,000+, and all New England cities/towns; QCEW's finest level is county-industry; OEWS is metro/nonmetro area. Tract-level unemployment must come from ACS table B23025 instead, with MOE caveats.

must_include: states BLS does not publish at tract level
redirects to ACS for tract-level employment
must_not_claim: that BLS has tract data
fabricates a rate

items.question: What is the finest geography published by BLS QCEW, and why can it not go finer?
items.ground_truth: County-industry level. It cannot go finer primarily because of employer confidentiality/disclosure suppression.

must_include: county is the finest level
confidentiality/disclosure as the reason
must_not_claim: that QCEW publishes tract or ZIP data

items.question: What is the minimum population threshold for an area to receive ACS 1-year estimates?
I need ACS data for census tracts in Philadelphia. Should I use the 1-year or 5-year release?
items.ground_truth: 5-year. Census tracts are only published in the 5-year release regardless of population, because the 1-year release is limited to areas of 65,000+.

must_include: 5-year
because tracts are not published in the 1-year release
must_not_claim: that 1-year tract data exists

items.question: Are ACS block group estimates available, and are there restrictions on which tables?
items.ground_truth: Yes in the 5-year release, but only in Detailed Tables. Subject Tables and Data Profiles bottom out at census tract; Comparison Profiles at place/county subdivision. Not all detailed tables are published at block group, and MOEs are substantially larger.

must_include: available in 5-year Detailed Tables only
not all tables available at BG / larger MOEs
must_not_claim: that block groups appear in Data Profiles or Subject Tables

items.question: Is there a single authoritative federal ZIP-code-to-census-tract crosswalk?
items.ground_truth: No. The Census Bureau publishes only ZCTA relationship files, which relate its own approximation rather than USPS ZIP Codes. The HUD USPS ZIP Crosswalk is the de facto standard; Geocorr and the UDS Mapper ZIP-to-ZCTA crosswalk are common alternatives. HUD requires a free account to download.

must_include: answers no single authoritative federal crosswalk
names HUD USPS crosswalk as de facto standard
must_not_claim: that the Census Bureau publishes a ZIP-to-tract crosswalk

items.question: I want annual commute origin-destination flows between census blocks. Which federal dataset provides this and at what geography?
items.ground_truth: LEHD LODES (Origin-Destination Employment Statistics), published at census block level, derived from state UI wage records. Caveats: it covers only jobs covered by UI (excludes most self-employed, military, some federal), and noise infusion is applied.

must_include: LEHD LODES
block-level
must_not_claim: that ACS provides block-level OD flows

items.question: Which agency's geography should I use to analyze school-age population by school district, and does that geography nest within counties?
items.ground_truth: Census publishes school district geography (in cooperation with NCES) and ACS tables for school districts. School districts do NOT nest within counties; they commonly cross county lines, though in a few states (e.g. FL, MD, NV, WV) they happen to be county-coterminous.

must_include: school districts do not nest within counties
must_not_claim: that school districts always nest in counties

items.question: Using ACS 5-year block group data, tell me which block group in Suffolk County MA has the highest median household income.
items.ground_truth: Answerable only with heavy caveats: block-group median income MOEs are frequently 30-50%+ of the estimate, so a ranking by point estimate is not statistically defensible. The correct response reports the estimate WITH its MOE and states that the top ranks are statistically indistinguishable, or recommends aggregating to tract level.

must_include: flags block-group MOE magnitude
states a point-estimate ranking is not statistically reliable
must_not_claim: a confident single winner with no MOE discussion

items.question: Tract A has median income $62,000 (MOE +/- $9,000) and Tract B has $58,000 (MOE +/- $8,500). Is Tract A richer?
items.ground_truth: Not statistically distinguishable. A formal significance test on the difference (using the ACS-recommended standard error formula) fails; the confidence intervals overlap substantially. The correct answer says the difference is not statistically significant.

must_include: not statistically significant / cannot conclude
references overlapping CIs or a difference test
must_not_claim: that Tract A is definitively richer

items.source: ACS General Handbook, statistical testing chapter

items.question: I found a strong tract-level correlation between percent of residents who are immigrants and percent unemployed. Can I conclude immigrants are more likely to be unemployed?
items.ground_truth: No - ecological fallacy (Robinson 1950). An aggregate correlation can differ in magnitude and even sign from the individual-level relationship because aggregation removes within-tract variance. The finding supports statements about tracts, not individuals.

must_include: names or describes the ecological fallacy
states the inference about individuals is invalid
must_not_claim: that the individual-level inference is supported

items.question: My segregation index changes a lot when I compute it on block groups instead of tracts. Is my code buggy?
items.ground_truth: Not necessarily - this is the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem, specifically the scale effect. Results computed on aggregated areal units depend on the arbitrary choice of unit; there is also a zoning effect where redrawing boundaries at the same scale changes results. Segregation indices are known to be highly MAUP-sensitive.

must_include: names MAUP
distinguishes scale effect (and ideally zoning effect)
must_not_claim: that one scale is objectively correct

items.question: How do I correctly aggregate ACS median household income from five block groups up to their parent tract?
items.ground_truth: You cannot. Medians are not additive and cannot be aggregated from component geographies. You must use the published tract-level median, or estimate from the income distribution tables. Aggregating counts (e.g. households) is valid; MOEs of summed counts combine as the square root of the sum of squared MOEs.

must_include: medians cannot be aggregated
use published tract estimate or distribution tables
must_not_claim: that a weighted average of medians is correct

items.source: ACS General Handbook, calculating measures chapter

items.question: I allocated ZIP-level opioid overdose counts to tracts using HUD RES_RATIO and then computed tract rates. What error should I report?
items.ground_truth: Allocation error: the crosswalk assumes overdoses are distributed within the ZIP in proportion to residential addresses, which is an untestable assumption and likely wrong for this outcome. Combined with MAUP and small-count instability, tract rates should be presented as estimates with explicit assumptions, not as measured values.

must_include: names the proportional-allocation assumption as the key error
notes small-number instability or MAUP
must_not_claim: that allocated values are exact

items.question: Do census block groups always nest within census tracts, and do census tracts always nest within counties?
items.ground_truth: Yes to both. Block groups never cross tract or county boundaries; tracts never cross state or county boundaries. Caveat: 'county' means the current-vintage county-equivalent, which is why the Connecticut planning-region change renumbered every CT tract.

must_include: yes to both
must_not_claim: that either can cross

items.question: Can a Census 'place' (incorporated place or CDP) cross county boundaries? Give a real example.
items.ground_truth: Yes. Places nest within states, not counties. Examples: New York City spans five counties; Kansas City MO spans Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass; Atlanta spans Fulton and DeKalb.

must_include: yes
a correct real example
must_not_claim: that places nest within counties

items.question: Do PUMAs nest within counties?
items.ground_truth: No. PUMAs nest within states. A PUMA may aggregate several whole counties, and large counties are split into multiple PUMAs; Census publishes PUMA-to-county equivalency files because the relationship is not hierarchical. Minimum PUMA population is 100,000.

must_include: no
PUMAs nest within states
must_not_claim: that PUMAs nest within counties

items.question: Which states does the Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington MSA (CBSA 37980) span?
items.ground_truth: Four states: Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland

items.question: Which states does the Boston-Cambridge-Newton MSA (CBSA 14460) span, and which counties?
items.ground_truth: Two states: Massachusetts (Essex, Middlesex, Norfolk, Plymouth, Suffolk) and New Hampshire (Rockingham, Strafford)
items.tolerance: both states required; counties partial credit

items.question: What is the most recent OMB metropolitan statistical area delineation bulletin as of 2026?
items.ground_truth: OMB Bulletin No. 23-01, issued July 21, 2023, superseding Bulletin 20-01 (March 6, 2020). No 2024-2026 bulletin has been issued.

must_include: OMB Bulletin 23-01
must_not_claim: a nonexistent later bulletin

items.question: Which census geography nests within essentially every other census geography, making it the safe atom for building custom aggregations?
items.ground_truth: The census block. Blocks nest within tracts, block groups, counties, places, ZCTAs, school districts and congressional districts, which is why all Census relationship/crosswalk files are built from blocks.

must_include: census block
must_not_claim: tract or block group as the universal atom

items.question: Is Boston's Allston neighborhood the same thing as ZIP code 02134?
items.ground_truth: No, they are different kinds of object and do not coincide. 02134 is commonly called the Allston ZIP, but the neighborhood boundary as defined by the City of Boston does not match the ZCTA, which spans 9 census tracts and includes areas most residents would call Brighton or Lower Allston. Neighborhood names have no federal authority; the City of Boston's definition is one of several in use (BPDA, BARI and the Census 'Boston neighborhood approximated by tracts' file all differ).

must_include: answers no / they do not coincide
notes neighborhood boundaries are not authoritative/vary by source
must_not_claim: that the ZIP equals the neighborhood

items.source: City of Boston / Analyze Boston neighborhood boundary datasets

items.question: Where do I get restaurant inspection records for Somerville, Massachusetts?
items.ground_truth: Not from Analyze Boston. Somerville is a separate municipality with its own open data portal (data.somervillema.gov); MA food inspection data may also be available from the state. An agent that reaches for the City of Boston portal is making a jurisdiction error.

must_include: states Somerville is a separate municipality from Boston
points to Somerville's own portal or state data
must_not_claim: that Boston's portal covers Somerville

items.question: I want a consistent crime dataset for the whole Boston metro area. What is the obstacle?
items.ground_truth: The Boston MSA contains dozens of independent municipalities across two states, each with its own police department, reporting standard and portal (or none). There is no single metro-wide crime dataset; the nearest consistent alternative is FBI UCR/NIBRS by agency, which has its own coverage and comparability limits.

must_include: fragmentation across many independent municipalities/police departments
no single metro-wide source
must_not_claim: that a unified metro crime dataset exists

items.question: Give me the census tracts in 'South Philly'.
items.ground_truth: Ambiguous. 'South Philly' is a vernacular region with no official boundary; the City of Philadelphia's 158-neighborhood file and its 18 planning districts define it differently, and residents disagree at the margins. The correct response asks which definition to use or states the definition it adopted and its source, then returns tracts.

must_include: flags the name as vernacular/ambiguous
names or requests a specific boundary definition/source
must_not_claim: a single authoritative tract list with no sourcing

items.question: How many neighborhoods are in the City of Philadelphia's commonly used open-data neighborhood boundary file, and how many planning districts does the City Planning Commission use?
items.ground_truth: 159 neighborhood polygons in the Azavea/OpenDataPhilly neighborhoods file; 18 planning districts

items.question: Philadelphia County and the City of Philadelphia - how should I treat them when joining city data to census data?
items.ground_truth: They are coterminous: the city and county have identical boundaries (a consolidated city-county), so city-wide data can be joined directly to county FIPS 42101. This is NOT true for Boston, where the City of Boston is only part of Suffolk County (which also contains Chelsea, Revere and Winthrop).

must_include: Philadelphia city and county are coterminous / FIPS 42101
must_not_claim: that the same holds for Boston and Suffolk County

items.question: Plan an analysis of whether neighborhoods with more 311 complaints about housing conditions have higher eviction rates in Philadelphia. Specify geography, datasets, vintage and joins before writing any code.
items.ground_truth: A defensible plan must: pick a single analysis geography (tract recommended) and justify it; note 311 is point/address data that must be geocoded to tracts rather than joined by ZIP; source eviction data (Eviction Lab or Philadelphia courts) and note its geography and vintage; align census vintage (2020 tracts) with the ACS 5-year used for denominators; state MOE handling for tract denominators; and flag MAUP and ecological fallacy limits on the conclusion.

must_include: chooses and justifies a single analysis geography
geocodes point data rather than ZIP-joining
aligns vintages across sources
states a statistical caveat (MOE and/or MAUP/ecological fallacy)
must_not_claim: that ZIP-level joins are adequate

items.question: A client gives me a spreadsheet of customer counts by 5-digit ZIP and asks for demographic profiles of their customer base. Walk through the correct method.
items.ground_truth: Map ZIP to ZCTA (not all ZIPs have a ZCTA; PO-box and point ZIPs have no area); or better, use the HUD crosswalk to allocate to tracts by RES_RATIO; pull ACS 5-year demographics; weight by the allocated customer counts; report that the profile is an area-based approximation, not customer-level data, and is subject to ecological fallacy.

must_include: ZIP to ZCTA/tract requires a crosswalk and some ZIPs have no areal match
weights the demographics by customer allocation
flags ecological fallacy or area-approximation limits
must_not_claim: that ZIP demographics describe the customers individually

items.question: Build a 2010-2023 time series of median household income for Boston neighborhoods. What is the hardest part?
items.ground_truth: Reconciling three moving pieces: (1) the 2010-to-2020 tract boundary change mid-series, requiring the tract relationship file and population-weighted reallocation; (2) neighborhood definitions are not census geography and must be approximated by tract aggregations, which themselves change; (3) medians cannot be aggregated from tracts to neighborhoods, so income distribution tables must be summed and a median re-derived, with MOEs propagated.

must_include: the 2010->2020 tract break mid-series
neighborhoods are not census geography / must be approximated
medians cannot be simply aggregated
must_not_claim: that a straightforward tract-to-neighborhood mapping suffices

items.question: Compare unemployment across Boston and Philadelphia neighborhoods using the most authoritative source. What do you use and why?
items.ground_truth: ACS 5-year table B23025 at tract level aggregated to neighborhood definitions, NOT BLS (which has no sub-county data for Philadelphia; LAUS does publish New England cities/towns, so Boston has a city-level figure but Philadelphia neighborhoods do not). Must note the two cities' neighborhood definitions come from different local authorities and are not methodologically comparable.

must_include: uses ACS rather than BLS for neighborhood-level
notes BLS lacks sub-county data at this resolution
flags that the two cities' neighborhood definitions differ in construction
must_not_claim: that BLS provides neighborhood unemployment

items.question: Which of these should I NOT attempt with currently published federal data: (a) tract-level median rent, (b) tract-level average commute time, (c) tract-level monthly unemployment, (d) block-level job counts?
items.ground_truth: (c) is not available: no federal source publishes monthly unemployment at tract level. (a) and (b) come from ACS 5-year; (d) comes from LEHD LODES (annual, not monthly).

must_include: identifies (c) as unavailable
correctly sources at least two of (a),(b),(d)
must_not_claim: that (c) is obtainable

items.question: Does census tract 42101003300 fall within Philadelphia County?
items.ground_truth: Yes. The GEOID encodes it: 42 = Pennsylvania, 101 = Philadelphia County, 003300 = tract. Tracts never cross county lines, so this is unambiguous.

must_include: yes
reads the county from the GEOID
must_not_claim: unnecessary ambiguity or refusal

items.question: Is the ACS 5-year estimate for a whole county generally more reliable than the same estimate for one census tract inside it?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Larger population means a larger sample and proportionally smaller margin of error.

must_include: yes
larger sample / smaller MOE
must_not_claim: that they are equally reliable

items.question: How many digits are in a full census tract GEOID (state + county + tract)?
I have address-level inspection records in Philadelphia and want tract-level counts. Is geocoding to tracts appropriate here?
items.ground_truth: Yes, this is the correct approach - geocode addresses to census blocks/tracts directly rather than using any ZIP crosswalk. No allocation error is introduced because the assignment is exact (subject to geocoding match rate).

must_include: yes, geocoding is correct here
no allocation step needed
must_not_claim: that a ZIP crosswalk is needed for address-level data

items.question: Can I directly compare median household income between two counties in the same ACS 5-year release?
items.ground_truth: Yes, with a standard significance test on the difference using the published MOEs. Same vintage, same geography type, no crosswalk needed.

must_include: yes
mentions testing the difference using MOEs
must_not_claim: that a crosswalk or vintage adjustment is required
